description: The Israeli Ministry of Transport publishes the GIS layers of its planning division on the national open data portal. Contents: 23 shapefile datasets, including existing and statutorily approved heavy rail passenger stations, heavy rail and light rail tunnels, road tunnels and light rail depots, the rail strategic plan's lines and stations to 2040, forecast morning peak rail passenger flows for 2040 from the national model, hourly rail frequencies (2019, 2020 and 2026), peak-hour boardings and alightings by station (September 2020), average bus speeds in morning and evening peaks (November 2021), bus terminals, bus priority lane completion, and the national outline plans TMA 3 (roads compilation, interchanges and detailed road plans) and TMA 42 (integrated land transport infrastructure: interchanges, tunnelling, grade-separated crossings, integrated transport centres). Producer: the ministry's planning division, with sources such as Israel Railways and the national transport model. Coverage: Israel, current network and plans to 2040. Format and access: shapefile, KML and CSV downloads with metadata spreadsheets through data.gov.il and its CKAN API. Licence: CC BY for most layers, other open terms for some. Free. Caveats: many layers were last refreshed in 2024 or earlier, plan layers show statutory or strategic intent, not built assets, and field names are in Hebrew. Simulation uses: rail and road network geometry with frequencies and demand for transit assignment, future network scenarios, and tunnel and interchange exposure studies. Related records: Israel active and planned cellular antenna sites (data-israel-moep-cellular-antenna-sites) come from the same portal.
